subject: Pen test inventory & boundary questions for Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: 2026-12-01T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Pen test scope — need clear mapping of hosting models

Jordan,

Thanks for taking this on. Our security team is scheduling an external penetration test for Acme’s integration with Redwood. Before we finalize the engagement letter we need a clear inventory that maps which endpoints and environments are in-scope under each hosting model: Hosted API, Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved pools), Private/VPC, and any on-prem package. Specifically we need:

- A list of public and private endpoints (API, admin, telemetry, metrics) and which party manages them.
- Network boundaries: which IP ranges or load balancers are customer-facing vs Redwood-internal.
- Which hosts/VMs/containers (or images) are considered Redwood-managed and excluded from customer PT, and which are tenant-side or customer-managed and in-scope.
- Any documented exclusions (e.g., hypervisor, OCI control plane, ephemeral build infrastructure).
- Evidence: asset inventory CSV, current network diagram, and recent remediation notes if there were prior findings.

We are aiming to start the test week of Dec 13; please let me know if Redwood can provide the inventory and any temporary test credentials by Dec 4 so we can publish the engagement scope to the vendor.

Appreciate the help — I can jump on a quick call if helpful.

—Alex Turner
Head of Security Operations
Acme Corporation
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T10:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pen test scope — need clear mapping of hosting models

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Mina (Security) and Aditya (Infra) to provide the asset mapping and diagrams. Attached is a small inventory template we use to respond to third-party PT requests, plus a high-level prod endpoint map to start the conversation.

High-level clarifications up front (short answers):
- Hosted API: fully Redwood-managed control plane and compute. Public API endpoints and our edge load balancers are Redwood-managed and will be in-scope for network-level testing, but we generally exclude Redwood internal build systems and CI/CD hosts.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): compute is dedicated to the customer but still managed by Redwood. Customer traffic flows through the same public API endpoints unless they use a private endpoint; for PT scope we typically include the tenant-facing service endpoints and any tenant metadata endpoints, and exclude Redwood tenant-hosting hypervisors and internal admin consoles unless explicitly requested.
- Private / VPC: there are two common variants — (1) Redwood control plane with customer-managed networking (customer VPC) and (2) fully on-prem package where both control plane and compute live inside customer network. For the VPC option, host-level assets inside the customer VPC are typically in-scope for the customer-run test; Redwood will provide a list of control-plane endpoints and our responsibilities.

Mina / Aditya — can you confirm the detailed asset lists, include any known exclusions, and share the network boundary diagram + a short remediation/status note for recent items? Alex, we’ll aim to get you a consolidated CSV and diagrams by EOD Dec 3 or Dec 4 latest.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T11:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pen test scope — need clear mapping of hosting models

Alex / Jordan — attaching the requested artifacts: pt-scope-asset-list.csv (inventory exported from our asset catalog) and network-boundary-diagram.png (high level). A few implementation notes and explicit scope bullets to avoid ambiguity for the vendor:

1) Hosted (Redwood API): in-scope
   - Public API edge endpoints (api.redwood.com) and associated CDN/edge LB DNS records.
   - Customer-facing admin consoles (if the customer uses Redwood Console for their account).
   - Excluded: Redwood internal CI/CD runners, build artifact stores, and internal monitoring/control-plane hosts not reachable from customer networks.

2) Dedicated (reserved pools): in-scope for tenant-facing components only
   - Tenant-facing service endpoints, model inference endpoints, and tokenization/ingestion proxies.
   - Excluded by default: physical host OS, hypervisor, and Redwood platform management plane (unless Acme requests host-level testing).

3) Private / VPC and On-Prem variants: scope depends on deployment model
   - VPC with Redwood control-plane: in-scope includes customer VPC subnets that host data-plane instances; Redwood will enumerate control-plane endpoints (management APIs) and indicate which interfaces are Redwood-managed vs customer-managed.
   - Fully on-prem: we will provide a dedicated asset list for the on-prem package; however, the customer-run PT will typically cover host/network assets that are physically inside customer networks.

4) Temporary test credentials / network access
   - We can issue short-lived read-only accounts for the Console and a test API key for the vendor (scoped to non-production models) — see note in the attached CSV column "test_creds_available".

5) Recent remediation note
   - There was a low severity logging misconfiguration in a hosted edge service discovered Oct 2026; remediation completed Nov 18, 2026. We have an internal post-mortem and can share sanitized excerpts with the vendor under NDA.

Action items:
- Jordan: confirm attachments shared to Acme’s secure Drive (done).
- Mina: produce final consolidated CSV with explicit endpoint owner column and deliver by EOD Dec 4.
- Aditya: prepare a short bullet list of excluded infra and provide IP ranges for public LBs by Dec 4.

If the vendor wants to test host-level components in Dedicated or On-Prem, we will set up a scoping call to align on safe testing rules and maintenance windows.

Regards,

Mina Haddad
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
Attachments: pt-scope-asset-list.csv, network-boundary-diagram.png
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pen test scope — need clear mapping of hosting models

Alex — confirming we delivered the asset CSV and diagrams to your secure Drive link (see related links). Mina and Aditya completed the outstanding items: final inventory includes an explicit "owner" column (Redwood vs Customer) and the IP ranges for the public load balancers are listed in the CSV.

Next steps for Acme / vendor:
- Review the CSV and diagram; if you need host-level testing for Dedicated, send a formal request and we will schedule a scoping call (Jira: SUP-4821).
- If you accept the default exclusions, vendor can proceed to vendor onboarding and we will provide the short-lived test creds by Dec 7.
- Mina will provide the sanitized post-mortem excerpt under NDA for the earlier logging issue if needed.

Please confirm whether the vendor will request host/hypervisor level testing or will accept the default scope. Once you confirm, we can finalize the engagement letter.

Thanks,
